description: Trade Postmortem Wave C (WC-K current-report read API, WC-N per-trade frontend, WC-O observability) traceability manifest. Reuses the j4b3_traceability_helper.py static/runtime validation framework established for Sprint 3A rather than introducing a competing schema.

requirements.title: Canonical current-report route and authorization
requirements.expected_behavior: GET /api/paper-trading/{trade_id}/current-report requires the same get_current_user_id dependency as every other paper-trading route; a trade belonging to another user is byte-for-byte indistinguishable (identical 404) from a nonexistent trade_id.

requirements.title: Feature-disabled behavior returns FEATURE_DISABLED, never a fabricated 404 or leaked report
requirements.expected_behavior: Evaluated strictly after ownership; an owned trade with the backend flag off always returns availability=FEATURE_DISABLED with every READY-only field null, even if a 1.2.0 report already exists.

requirements.title: All seven governed availability states are mapped deterministically
requirements.expected_behavior: READY, PROCESSING, NOT_ELIGIBLE, NOT_AVAILABLE, TERMINAL_FAILURE, INTEGRITY_CONTRADICTION, FEATURE_DISABLED cover every reachable combination of trade status/outbox status/report existence.

requirements.title: Current-version identity derivation, never a fuzzy/latest lookup
requirements.expected_behavior: The read path derives the exact governed (schema_version, calculation_version, rules_version) triple via current_target_identity, the same primitive the write path uses.

requirements.title: Side-effect-free GET — never generates, claims, or mutates
requirements.expected_behavior: GET never calls process_current_report, never acquires provider evidence, never claims/settles/inserts/updates an outbox row, never mutates a trade row.

requirements.title: Deterministic serialization for a fixed persisted report
requirements.expected_behavior: Repeated GETs of the identical persisted report return byte-identical response bodies.

requirements.title: Canonical JSON persistence and evidence hash
requirements.expected_behavior: One authoritative recursive canonicalizer for all six persisted report JSON fields; persist_report canonicalizes each exactly once and reuses those exact collections for both hashing and the INSERT payload.

requirements.title: Governed source manifest — required fields and historical optionality
requirements.expected_behavior: has_entry_snapshot/has_exit_snapshot/exit_evidence_rules_version/phase1_calculation_version/attribution_rules_version required on every Sprint-2+ report; price_path_calculation_version genuinely absent (not null) on a historical/non-enhanced row.

requirements.title: Governed claim/evidence vocabularies — no privacy leak of raw error codes
requirements.expected_behavior: evidence_class/confidence_band/source_type/verification_level/freshness_status use the authoritative shared Enums directly; a raw outbox error code is never leaked to the client.

requirements.title: Claim semantics enforcement, shared not duplicated
requirements.expected_behavior: The one authoritative rule check, called by both the frozen dataclass validator and PostmortemClaimModel's Pydantic validator.

requirements.title: Referential integrity between claims and evidence
requirements.expected_behavior: Public helper (renamed from _validate_merged_evidence_integrity), reused identically by build_report_payload and the READY conversion boundary; a dangling supporting/opposing evidence reference fails closed.

requirements.title: Typed structured_report.price_path.version_and_provenance (A4)
requirements.expected_behavior: The exact 9-field 1.2.0 governed provenance subtree is typed (extra=forbid); malformed/missing subtree fails closed to INTEGRITY_CONTRADICTION; unrelated structured_report/price_path sections are preserved via extra=allow.

requirements.title: Supersession proof (A5)
requirements.expected_behavior: supersedes_report_id is null with no predecessor; a real predecessor's EXACT stored id is echoed (never recalculated); repeated GET causes no insert/update/repair.

requirements.title: Persisted version-provenance inventory closure
requirements.expected_behavior: Every version/provenance value the API can expose is typed, semantically validated, and sourced from the exact immutable persisted report; optional historical values are never synthesized; linked provider-manifest expansion recorded as nonblocking backlog.

requirements.title: Fail-closed malformed persistence behavior
requirements.expected_behavior: A ValidationError or ReportIntegrityError constructing the READY response is caught, logs only privacy-safe metadata, and converts to INTEGRITY_CONTRADICTION; never a raw 500 or leaked content; causes no mutation or self-repair.

requirements.title: Exact TypeScript contract mirroring the frozen backend response
requirements.expected_behavior: Governed fields typed exactly (never any); TriggerTimingVerification/JSONValue/EXTERNAL_UNOFFICIAL_DAILY match the backend's governed vocabularies; compile-time assertions reject unsupported values.

requirements.title: Authenticated read-only client
requirements.expected_behavior: Reuses the shared axios instance's Supabase JWT interceptor; never invokes a report-generation POST endpoint from the read page.

requirements.title: Bounded polling stops on request error, not just non-PROCESSING data
requirements.expected_behavior: refetchInterval checks q.state.status==='error' first (stale PROCESSING data must not mask a failed subsequent request); refetchOnWindowFocus/refetchOnReconnect disabled so neither bypasses the bound.

requirements.expected_behavior: The signal threaded to fetchCurrentPostmortemReport actually becomes aborted (not merely ignored) on unmount and on a trade-ID change.

requirements.expected_behavior: Every non-READY state gets a named, explicit message; never a blank page for a state the backend deliberately distinguishes.

requirements.expected_behavior: COMPLETE renders outcome/P&L/exit mechanism/MFE-MAE/touch evidence/claims/evidence/gaps/warnings/provenance; LIMITED_EVIDENCE is visually distinct, never implies certainty, shows the canonical insufficient-evidence sentence unchanged.

requirements.expected_behavior: IN→₹, US→$, unrecognized market shows the number without a fabricated symbol; percentages never carry a currency symbol; closure classification sourced ONLY from the governed EXIT/closure_classification evidence item, N/A when absent.

requirements.expected_behavior: A separate disclosure from version/provenance using only explicitly typed source_manifest fields; price_path_calculation_version's row is omitted (never a fabricated null) when historically absent.

requirements.title: Evidence-value safety and accessibility
requirements.expected_behavior: Bounded JSON formatting for non-scalar evidence values (never [object Object], never dangerouslySetInnerHTML); observation_timestamp/limitations shown when present; contradiction_flags labelled distinctly; status/alert roles and aria-expanded on disclosures.

requirements.expected_behavior: Exactly one View Postmortem link on a closed trade, gated by the frontend flag; never rendered on an open trade; never a second Buy/Sell/Close control; no duplicate after rerender.

requirements.title: Frontend feature gate, tests, typecheck, production build
requirements.expected_behavior: Independent of the daily-report flag; backend capability remains authoritative even when this flag is on. Full suite/typecheck/build all green.
nodes: TradePostmortemPage — feature-disabled frontend gate > renders a safe unavailable state and never calls the API when the frontend flag is off

requirements.title: Browser-smoke scope and honest limitation
requirements.implementation: N/A (manual verification against a temporary dev server)
requirements.expected_behavior: Feature-disabled route, invalid-trade-ID route, unauthenticated-user route, and mobile layout verified live with zero console errors; READY/LIMITED_EVIDENCE states explicitly recorded as unverified live (no safe mock/interception mechanism in this environment) and covered instead by WC-N-06's component tests.

requirements.title: Metrics-store fail-open behavior
requirements.expected_behavior: Every safe_* function never raises regardless of an internal store failure; an unrecognized availability value produces one bounded warning, never a propagated KeyError.

requirements.title: Logging-subsystem fail-open behavior
requirements.expected_behavior: A broken logging handler/subsystem must never propagate out of any safe_* function, _log_internal_failure_bounded, or any observability log.warning/log.info call in current_report_generation.py/outbox_worker.py.

requirements.title: Provider attempt/success/failure/replay signals and timing
requirements.expected_behavior: Real acquisition success/failure record exactly one attempt plus one success/failure; compatible-evidence replay records zero attempts and no duration sample; a metrics/logging failure never changes the FAILED_RETRYABLE outcome.

requirements.title: Queue-health snapshot: counts, ages, version isolation, pre-claim observation, no mutation
requirements.expected_behavior: Exact status counts and version isolation; active-vs-expired lease classification; documented age semantics (created_at/claimed_at/last_attempt_at, never next_attempt_at); >120s-in-GENERATING count; null ages/zero counts when empty; read before the claim each cycle; causes zero mutation.

requirements.title: Noise-bounded logging: heartbeat and transition/reminder warnings
requirements.expected_behavior: Heartbeat at most every 5 minutes; warnings on zero-to-non-zero/increase/15-minute-reminder, reset on return to zero; deterministic via an injectable clock.

requirements.title: Process-local / multi-replica limitations, disclosed honestly
requirements.expected_behavior: QueueHealthLogState resets on every genuinely new worker task start (not the idempotent early-return) and on process restart; each replica maintains independent state (no cross-replica dedup) — documented explicitly, not silently assumed.

requirements.title: Real EXPLAIN evidence for the queue-health query
requirements.expected_behavior: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON) captured at a representative beta-scale row count (5,000) on both PostgreSQL 15 and 17, never asserting a brittle plan node or millisecond threshold; EXPLAIN ANALYZE itself causes zero mutation.

requirements.title: Log-volume analysis and query-cost evidence documentation
requirements.expected_behavior: Realistic log-volume estimate (GET traffic 1:1 with metrics lines, no cap; worker heartbeat/warnings bounded); the 'query is cheap' claim replaced with measured EXPLAIN evidence and an honest, evidence-supported capacity boundary (no unsupported 50,000-row threshold).

requirements.title: Controlled remediation procedure, no ad hoc production SQL
requirements.expected_behavior: The ad hoc 'manually reset FAILED_TERMINAL to PENDING' instruction is replaced with a 9-step controlled procedure (disable if material, read-only evidence, root-cause fix, reviewed script, owner approval, dry-run, transactional execution, consistency verification, audit retention). No remediation tool built without a real unresolved case.

requirements.title: Evidence-based global-beta boundary and enablement/disablement/rollback procedures
requirements.expected_behavior: services/auth.py inspected — no invite/cohort gate exists; beta boundary stated honestly as a global, low-traffic activation, not a restricted cohort; frontend-enabled/backend-disabled correctly documented as FEATURE_DISABLED (never a fabricated 404); dark deployment, enablement, disablement, and rollback are fully executable procedures.
